messages.content: I want to get some rest

function.name: uber_eat_order
function.description: Place an order for food from selected restaurants with specified items and their quantities. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

restaurants.description: The name of the restaurant from which the user wants to order food. Use the exact name as registered on Uber Eats.

items.description: A list of item names that the user wants to order from the restaurant.

quantities.description: A list of integers, each representing the quantity of the corresponding item in the order. The quantities should align with the items list by index.

message.content: Got it—take your time! Just let me know whenever you’re ready to pick up where we left off.
message.reasoning:
The user says "I want to get some rest". This seems like they might want to place an order? But no mention of ordering or specifying restaurant. They just say I want to get some rest. That could mean they want to take a break, maybe not wanting to do anything else right now.

We need to interpret what the user means. Possibly they want to cancel all orders? Or they want to stop interacting?

But we have only one tool available: placing an order. There's no tool for cancellation. So if there's nothing relevant, we can respond politely acknowledging them taking a break. We can't call the function because it's irrelevant. So we simply respond with something like:

"Sure thing! Let me know when you're ready to continue."

Thus we don't use the function.
